sources.title: Technical Results on the Convergence of Quasi-Newton Methods for Nonsmooth Optimization
sources.access: Publisher full theorem and proof HTML read; arXiv v1 cross-checked. Published numbering differs from arXiv cross-references.
locators: Published Lemmas 3.1-3.5 and Theorem 3.1; arXiv v1 main criticality cross-reference Theorem 3.10
Published Section 4 exploration theorem; arXiv v1 Theorem 4.15
Remark 3.1 / arXiv Remark 1 links normal space to VU theory and partial smoothness
sources.paraphrase: The criticality conclusion assumes an existing iterate limit and prescribed eigenvalue bounds and annihilation of active-gradient differences. A separate result describes local exploration of smooth pieces under additional matrix behavior. The geometric lemma converts linear dependence of a fully active nondegenerate family into criticality. These are conditional quasi-Newton results.

sources.title: Nonsmooth Variants of Powell’s BFGS Convergence Theorem
sources.access: Author preprint full theorem/proof text read; preprint title differs from journal title.
sources.paraphrase: Ordinary BFGS sequences use differentiable accepted points and Armijo–weak-Wolfe. Theorem 3.3 requires smooth positive-definite Hessians near the entire sequence closure; Corollary 3.6 yields a smooth-region result for semialgebraic strongly convex objectives. Theorem 4.1 uses exact smooth agreement on positive bands, and Corollary 4.2 proves Euclidean-norm convergence.
sources.version_note: Peer review 2026-09-11: bound theorem3.3/corollary3.6 locators explicitly to arXiv v1; journal manuscript uses different numbering. Earliest located Optimization Online date precedes arXiv by one day.

sources.title: A simple Newton method for local nonsmooth optimization
sources.access: Full arXiv theorem and proof text read. No journal publication established; Gebken 2026 still cites this as arXiv (2019).
locators: Propositions 5.5-5.6 and their proofs, pp. 15-16 in PDF one-based pagination
sources.paraphrase: Affine independence and strict positive multipliers are standard nondegeneracy conditions. Nearby multiplier estimates remain unique and positive by linear-system stability. The convergence theorem concerns a bundle Newton method with second-order oracle information and a full initial bundle, not unmodified BFGS.

sources.title: Active Sets, Nonsmoothness, and Sensitivity
sources.first_public_date: 2002-11-14 (electronic publication; earlier public draft not established)
sources.access: Author-hosted journal PDF theorem and proof text read.
sources.paraphrase: The subgradient affine hull and active-manifold normal space already organize partial smoothness. Under the stated sharpness and regularity assumptions, zero in the subgradient affine hull is equivalent to criticality of the restriction to the active manifold. The paper provides calculus and sensitivity results, not a general full-BFGS convergence theorem.

sources.title: Partial smoothness and constant rank
sources.journal_date: Published successor: 2022-03-17 online; SIAM Journal on Optimization 32(1), 276-291
sources.access: 2018 two-author preprint theorem/proof text read; 2022 three-author successor publisher metadata checked. No equality of theorem numbering or every statement across versions is assumed.
sources.paraphrase: Partial smoothness of the subdifferential is expressed through constant rank and related to identification. The identification implication uses convergence of both points and appropriate subgradients to the reference graph point. Those premises are not supplied merely by differentiable BFGS iterates approaching a kink.

sources.title: Clarke Subgradients of Stratifiable Functions
sources.access: ArXiv full proof text read; publisher metadata checked. Locators refer to the 14-page arXiv version.
locators: Corollary 9 proof and its cited smooth definable critical-value argument
sources.paraphrase: A compatible finite definable Whitney stratification gives a common tangential projection for all Clarke subgradients. The paper states finite Clarke critical values. Its projection formula also applies to affine combinations by linearity, allowing the affine-critical variant used here to be deduced as a corollary; that last deduction is this audit’s inference.

sources.title: Subdifferential Enlargements and Continuity Properties of the VU-Decomposition in Convex Optimization
sources.access: Author manuscript full relevant text read; publisher metadata checked. Filename is not used as proof of first-publication date.
locators: Publisher acknowledgments credit Alfredo N. Iusem for the two Remark 3.2 counterexamples
sources.paraphrase: The VU spaces and common projected subgradient are established concepts. Affine hull formation preserves inner semicontinuity but can destroy outer semicontinuity, even for maximally monotone subgradient mappings. This is a direct antecedent to the report’s rank-loss warning; the report uses a different finite, strongly convex, semialgebraic example.

sources.paraphrase: Strong (a) regularity quantitatively controls tangential projections of nearby subgradients. The convergence applications concern perturbed subgradient and proximal methods, with noise, decreasing steps and genericity/boundedness qualifications. They do not establish deterministic ordinary full-BFGS convergence.

sources.title: Proximal Gradient VU-Method with Superlinear Convergence for Nonsmooth Convex Optimization
sources.access: Author manuscript Algorithm 3.1 and theorem/proof text read; publisher metadata checked. Earliest public manuscript date not established.
locators: Theorem 4.4 and proof, printed pp. 13-14; condition (4.2)
sources.paraphrase: The algorithm performs a proximal-gradient step followed by a U-space correction. Theorem 3.3 assumes bounded correction matrices and step controls, concluding that accumulation points minimize. Its superlinear theorem adds positive U-curvature, relative-interior nondegeneracy and a Dennis-Moré-type condition. This is a different method from unmodified full BFGS.

claims.statement: The affine subgradient hull equals a+V with a perpendicular to V; all subgradients share U-projection a. Nonzero a produces an equal-rate descent direction.
claims.comparison: The report’s definitions are the established VU geometry, followed by elementary orthogonal projection and rescaling. The implication from one optimal cluster point to objective/distance convergence is a standard compactness and monotonicity deduction.
claims.open_search_limits: No finite online search certifies novelty; unpublished, inaccessible, differently named, or unindexed equivalents may exist.

claims.statement: Pointwise affine-critical correctness need not give uniform positive affine separation on a compact positive band; F=u+u²+v²+|uv| is a finite strongly convex example.
claims.comparison: The general affine-hull semicontinuity failure is known. The exact two-variable example, global absence of false affine-critical points and positive-band separation failure were not located in the searched sources; these additional features should be described as an explicit refinement, not discovery of rank instability.
claims.confidence: high for known mechanism; moderate for exact-example search
claims.open_search_limits: No finite online search certifies novelty; unpublished, inaccessible, differently named, or unindexed equivalents may exist.

claims.statement: Affine independence and strictly positive optimal weights imply local affine-critical correctness and lower semicontinuity of the affine separation.
claims.comparison: Stable augmented gradient systems and positive barycentric coordinates directly yield the report’s argument. Missing active indices are handled by zero extension and positivity. Attribute the geometry; it does not establish ordinary BFGS convergence.
claims.open_search_limits: No finite online search certifies novelty; unpublished, inaccessible, differently named, or unindexed equivalents may exist.

claims.statement: A finite convex semialgebraic objective has finitely many affine-critical values, constant value on critical path classes/components, and a low-level gap.
claims.comparison: This is a straightforward corollary of established stratified projection/Sard machinery, although the exact affine-critical formulation was not found verbatim. The report provides a self-contained semialgebraic path proof. See the separate derivation below; merely citing finite Clarke critical values would be insufficient.
claims.confidence: high for corollary; not a claim of verbatim prior statement
claims.open_search_limits: No finite online search certifies novelty; unpublished, inaccessible, differently named, or unindexed equivalents may exist.

claims.statement: The general-dimensional finite C²,¹ smooth-max local convergence conjecture with weighted tangential curvature remains open in the report.
claims.comparison: No searched source proves the stated unmodified full-BFGS conclusion with arbitrary SPD initialization. Related structure-aware algorithms and conditional limit theorems do not close it.
claims.confidence: high for scope distinction; no universal open-problem certification
claims.open_search_limits: No finite online search certifies novelty; unpublished, inaccessible, differently named, or unindexed equivalents may exist.

claims.statement: In the plane, strict positive contours and regular smooth/two-branch structure away from affine criticality force an affine-critical cluster point of every admissible full-BFGS run.
claims.comparison: The report permits nonsmooth nonoptimal cluster candidates and derives its matrix contradiction without an iterate limit, fixed spectral bounds or a limiting eigenspace. This combination was not found in the closest works. It is conditional on an infinite differentiable accepted run, not an existence theorem for every exceptional search ray.
claims.open_search_limits: No finite online search certifies novelty; unpublished, inaccessible, differently named, or unindexed equivalents may exist.

claims.statement: Nondegenerate planar convex smooth maxima with strict positive contours have an objective-dependent convergence basin valid for arbitrary SPD initialization and every fixed valid Armijo–weak-Wolfe pair.
claims.comparison: The objective geometry overlaps standard smooth-max nondegeneracy; the unmodified BFGS run quantifier is the part not subsumed. The report proves convergence, not the quadratic rate of a bundle Newton algorithm.
claims.open_search_limits: No finite online search certifies novelty; unpublished, inaccessible, differently named, or unindexed equivalents may exist.

claims.statement: The affine-critical semialgebraic gap plus C’s structural assumptions gives a sufficiently low planar BFGS convergence basin without positive multipliers.
claims.comparison: The gap is known geometric machinery. The new candidate content is its combination with C’s dynamical theorem; semialgebraicity alone is explicitly insufficient.
claims.open_search_limits: No finite online search certifies novelty; unpublished, inaccessible, differently named, or unindexed equivalents may exist.

claims.statement: Corner level-velocities can be joined by a positive angular field w=h n+hθ T whose determinant transport costs O(d).
claims.comparison: The formula and tangential derivative cancellation are classical support-function algebra, even though C does not require h to be a convex support function. The gluing near the whole cluster set and O(d) transport from weak-Wolfe eligibility were not located as prior BFGS arguments.
claims.open_search_limits: No finite online search certifies novelty; unpublished, inaccessible, differently named, or unindexed equivalents may exist.

claims.statement: For fixed locally constant gradient-difference rank, a C¹ common-rate field exists on a compact non-affine-critical set, with bounded secant correction.
claims.comparison: This combines standard constant-rank/Gram formulas and partitions of unity with local convex smooth gradient estimates. It constructs visibility and correction, not the missing higher-dimensional transport or BFGS convergence.
claims.confidence: high for ingredients; exact packaged lemma not found
claims.open_search_limits: No finite online search certifies novelty; unpublished, inaccessible, differently named, or unindexed equivalents may exist.

claims.statement: For Q=diag(1,2,3), the canonical field ∇F/||∇F||² can fail the executed-step span relation on eligible pairs, despite full smoothness.
claims.comparison: This is a concrete obstruction to a particular certificate, not failure of BFGS or nonexistence of every certificate: a radial field works for the same quadratic. No exact published example was located.
claims.open_search_limits: No finite online search certifies novelty; unpublished, inaccessible, differently named, or unindexed equivalents may exist.

claims.statement: The explicit three quadratic branches with gradients (1,0),(0,1),(-1,-1) have a full-BFGS basin F(x0)<1/100.
claims.comparison: Strong convexity and positive-weight geometry belong to a standard test-function family. The coefficients, certified 1/100 basin and arbitrary-initial-matrix BFGS conclusion were not found in the searched literature.
claims.open_search_limits: No finite online search certifies novelty; unpublished, inaccessible, differently named, or unindexed equivalents may exist.

claims.statement: That quadratic maximum converges in the stated basin although the radial secant condition fails near curved interfaces on eligible pairs.
claims.comparison: The construction refutes the report’s particular RS sufficiency condition as a necessary condition. It is not an infinite divergent BFGS run, and it is not by itself a separation from every published convergence criterion.
claims.open_search_limits: No finite online search certifies novelty; unpublished, inaccessible, differently named, or unindexed equivalents may exist.

claims.statement: Every infinite admissible full-BFGS run converges globally for max_i(a_i u²+b_i v), a_i>0 and slopes of both signs, with arbitrarily many essential branches including b_i=0.
claims.comparison: The class has curved switching parabolas and can have flat normal regions. Positive bands can contain nonsmooth points, excluding direct use of smooth-band agreement; repeated slopes at the optimizer need not form an affinely independent family. No exact theorem matching all run and line-search quantifiers was located.
claims.open_search_limits: No finite online search certifies novelty; unpublished, inaccessible, differently named, or unindexed equivalents may exist.

claims.statement: Piecewise exponential rescaling of (u,2v) cancels first-order transport across an arbitrary finite parabolic envelope.
claims.comparison: The envelope, determinant identities and Taylor bounds are standard tools. The branch constants k_i and compensated logarithmic transport estimate for this BFGS certificate were not found in the searched papers. This is analytical rescaling, not an algorithmic coordinate change.
claims.open_search_limits: No finite online search certifies novelty; unpublished, inaccessible, differently named, or unindexed equivalents may exist.

claims.statement: max{u²+v,3u²,2u²-v} converges under full BFGS but violates RS on eligible first-step families for every allowed line-search pair.
claims.comparison: The metrics vary with epsilon and certify separate accepted first steps. The claim is strict nonnecessity of an internal sufficient condition, not a common infinite bad history. The corrected rho construction handles c1>2/3.
claims.open_search_limits: No finite online search certifies novelty; unpublished, inaccessible, differently named, or unindexed equivalents may exist.

claims.statement: Strong convexity, a common tangential subgradient projection Lipschitz on an open convex neighborhood of the compact initial sublevel, and local C¹,¹ regularity off one exceptional hyperplane imply full-BFGS convergence, with arbitrary coupling and SPD initialization.
claims.comparison: The fixed tangent/normal split has established geometric antecedents. U derives matrix control and tolerates unbounded full-gradient Lipschitz constants near the plane; the cited conditional spectral and identification theorems do not supply this conclusion. Theorem 3.6 of DDJ supplies a further geometric antecedent: the report’s flat-interface Lipschitz projected-gradient property implies their local tangential strong-(a) estimate by A(x)-A(y). This is an inference, not an equality of complete hypotheses or algorithms.
claims.open_search_limits: No finite online search certifies novelty; unpublished, inaccessible, differently named, or unindexed equivalents may exist.

claims.statement: For a closed scalar exceptional set with genuine nonsmoothness on every parallel interface, a strongly convex objective with a Lipschitz tangential projection forces an affine-critical cluster point.
claims.comparison: No equivalent theorem was located for possibly countably many parallel interfaces and all admissible full-BFGS histories. The scalar closed-set and genuine-nondifferentiability assumptions matter; U.1 is not literally U.2 with E={0}.
claims.open_search_limits: No finite online search certifies novelty; unpublished, inaccessible, differently named, or unindexed equivalents may exist.

claims.statement: For psi(u,v)+h(v), tangential strong convexity plus strict positive contours can replace full strong convexity in the convergence argument.
claims.comparison: The split is a familiar composite/VU model and the projected curvature estimate uses known monotonicity and cocoercivity. No exact ordinary-BFGS theorem with this weaker normal-curvature regime was found. The 2025 proximal-gradient VU theorem uses a proximal step and U-correction, bounded matrices and, for superlinear rates, a Dennis-Moré condition; it does not transfer to this ordinary BFGS statement.
claims.open_search_limits: No finite online search certifies novelty; unpublished, inaccessible, differently named, or unindexed equivalents may exist.

claims.statement: A normal cutoff frame on the whole hypothetical cluster set has a tangential transport residual controlled by predicted decrease.
claims.comparison: Fixed subspace projections and cutoff construction are standard. The executed-step-plus-tangential-residual decomposition and its use with derived BFGS restricted growth were not identified in the searched literature.
claims.open_search_limits: No finite online search certifies novelty; unpublished, inaccessible, differently named, or unindexed equivalents may exist.

claims.statement: A dyadic integrable curvature-spike function yields all-dimensional full-BFGS convergence while RS fails in every optimizer neighborhood; exact complete-series formulas are available.
claims.comparison: Narrow positive bumps with summable masses are a standard real-analysis construction. The exact a_j^-3 height/a_j^5 width family and its BFGS/RS use were not located. RS failure is not absence of every possible prior transported certificate, and the function may still have partial smoothness along v=0.
claims.open_search_limits: No finite online search certifies novelty; unpublished, inaccessible, differently named, or unindexed equivalents may exist.

claims.statement: The coupled family 1/2(||u||²+v²)+|(1+cᵀu)v|+r(v), 0<||c||<1, cannot equal differentiable S(u,v)+h(v) near zero, while the stated BFGS local convergence and RS failure hold.
claims.comparison: The obstruction is the varying normal jump, proved by subtracting tangential values. It excludes one additive representation only, not nonlinear composite or partial-smooth representations. The correction c≠0 is essential for nonsplitting; c=0 explicitly splits.
claims.open_search_limits: No finite online search certifies novelty; unpublished, inaccessible, differently named, or unindexed equivalents may exist.
